label: explicit_diagnosis_compatible
rationale: SS is explicitly included in the pathological diagnoses for surgical magnesium-clip evaluation.
cohort_reconciliation: Both groups undergo en bloc tumor resection after standard chemotherapy. The intervention compares magnesium closure clips with electrocautery/suture ligation; control NO_INTERVENTION coding does not mean no surgery.
extra_biomarker_requirement: No molecular entry gate is stated.
protocol_uncertainty: Inclusion and metadata ages 18–65 conflict with a trailing 18–75 sentence in exclusions. Clinical and prior-study restrictions remain. External protocol and live availability are unknown; saved status is NOT_YET_RECRUITING. No hemostatic or oncologic benefit is established.
quotes: Diagnosis must be confirmed pathologically as osteosarcoma, synovial sarcoma, liposarcoma, or other bone and soft tissue sarcomas;
Must have undergone standard chemotherapy and require en bloc resection;

label: explicit_diagnosis_compatible
rationale: SS is explicitly named in conditions and compatible with broad refractory solid-tumor eligibility, including refusal of standard treatment.
cohort_reconciliation: SS falls within the general AOH1996 pathway. Part B NSCLC permits an EGFR TKI combination and stable disease or better on that drug for at least two months; that exception does not establish a combination route for SS.
extra_biomarker_requirement: No positive PCNA/Myc/gammaH2AX assay is required for SS in saved criteria. Exploratory pharmacodynamic measurements and the NSCLC EGFR-TKI exception are not SS biomarker gates.
protocol_uncertainty: Age at least 18, oral-drug tolerance, organ function and interacting-medication exclusions remain. External appendix/protocol and live cohort availability are unreviewed; only the single-agent arm is enumerated despite the combination objective.
quotes: Patients with solid tumors failing standard therapies or patients refusing standard treatments
Part B NSCLC combination (EGFR TKI + AOH1996) cohort: patients with stable disease or better on EGFR TKI for at least 2 months

label: explicit_diagnosis_compatible
rationale: SS is explicitly eligible for first-line advanced STS treatment; the excluded unsuitable histologies, including extraosseous myxoid chondrosarcoma, do not exclude SS.
cohort_reconciliation: AI with or without MASCT-I, requiring no prior advanced-disease chemotherapy/targeted treatment or progression after six months from neoadjuvant/adjuvant completion. Cumulative anthracycline exposure, prior cell/immunotherapy and planned surgery impose additional restrictions.
extra_biomarker_requirement: No explicit tumor antigen, fusion or HLA gate is stated for SS. Cell-product treatment does not itself establish a molecular entry criterion.
protocol_uncertainty: Age 18–70 and apheresis-related organ/blood requirements remain. External drug/product protocol and live availability are unverified. Commercial drug descriptions do not establish efficacy of MASCT-I or the combination.
quotes: No previous treatment with systematic chemotherapy or targeted therapy for advanced soft tissue sarcomas or whose disease progressed after 6months of the end of neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy.
Surgery for soft tissue sarcoma is planned during the study.

label: explicit_diagnosis_compatible
rationale: SS is explicitly named in conditions and compatible with the broad STS eligibility for definitive proton radiation.
cohort_reconciliation: Single inoperable-STS pathway, with multidisciplinary radiation feasibility assessment. Metastatic disease is not uniformly excluded but requires expected survival greater than two years. This differs from the separate preoperative PROSARC-1 record.
extra_biomarker_requirement: No molecular entry gate is stated. Genomic, blood and MRI biomarkers are exploratory investigations.
protocol_uncertainty: Age at least 18, travel to Bergen/Oslo, prior tumor-site radiation, cardiac-device and recent systemic-therapy restrictions remain. External protocol and live availability are unverified. Planned local-control improvement and radiation-dose rationale are hypotheses, not comparative results.
quotes: For patients with metastatic disease a life-expectancy greater than 2 years should be expected.
